headline: Katie Zacharia out as White House press secretary after first week on the job
author: Jennifer Jacobs, Kristin Brown, Stefan Becket, Kathryn Watson

paragraphs.text: S. officials told CBS News on Friday. Some White House staff learned about the change from news coverage.

The New York Times first reported that she had been fired as press secretary. CBS News reached out to Zacharia for comment, but she did not immediately reply. In a social media post Friday night, she wrote, "President Trump is a kind, wonderful, gracious, thoughtful, enthusiastic, and hardworking man.
I wish more Americans appreciated him. No one will ever make America great the way he has and continues to. It was an honor to work for him."
She was seen at the White House as recently as Friday morning. "They've been so nasty to her," Mr. Trump said, referring to the press.
"I said, to her, 'Honestly if I were you, I'd reconsider. You think about it. But I would reconsider.
You got a beautiful husband and family.' I met the family yesterday. Beautiful kids.
It's like from a picture postcard. I said, 'You should reconsider. '"The abrupt shift came one week to the day after Mr.

Trump announced Zacharia as his pick to replace Karoline Leavitt, who stepped aside in August. The White House has not yet indicated who may replace Zacharia. Zacharia's qualifications and background quickly came under scrutiny as questions arose over her résumé.

CBS News and other outlets reported that Zacharia has represented herself as a lawyer over the years. She graduated from Pepperdine Law School but failed the California bar exam in 2011, a fact she acknowledged on Thursday. ""I was very careful how I executed this.

In her first and only press briefing on Tuesday, a visibly nervous Zacharia spoke from prepared remarks for about 10 minutes before taking questions from just three outlets — Breitbart, Fox News and the Daily Mail — for another five. "What I feel is I really stepped up to the plate to do the press conference, Sean, with very little prep time," Zacharia told Fox News' Sean Hannity on Thursday. "I received briefing materials in the morning of Tuesday and I went to deliver all of the great results that President Trump is delivering for the American people that are not often spread in the national media."

"The about-face on Zacharia's role was reminiscent of the tenure of Anthony Scaramucci, who survived just 11 days as White House communications director during Mr. Trump's first term. "Records are made to be broken," Scaramucci said in a post on X.
"But I take no pleasure in other people's pain."
